literal: Those who possess learning by listening, which is food for the ear, are equal to those who are perfected by sacrificial food, on this earth.
translation: Those on earth who feast on learning through their ears are equal to the celestial beings who feed on sacrificial offerings.
modern: செவிக்கு உணவாகிய கேள்வி ஞானத்தைப் பெற்றவர்கள், இவ்வுலகில் வாழ்ந்தாலும், வேள்வித் தீயின் அவியுணவை உண்ணும் தேவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet elevates the status of those who acquire wisdom by listening. The poet compares the physical food of the gods, which is the sacrificial offering (அவியுணவு), to the intellectual food of humans, which is listening to wise words (செவியுணவு). Those who feed their ears with knowledge while living on this earth (நிலத்து) are considered equal to the immortal celestial beings (ஆன்றார்) who are sustained by sacrifices. Through this comparison, the act of listening to wisdom is shown to be a divine sustenance that elevates mortal humans to a god-like state.
